question.text: A Cat I/II AIF IM is comparing a 100% catch-up clause vs a 50% partial catch-up, all other terms equal. Which statement is MOST accurate from the LP's perspective?

answer.text: LPs prefer 100% catch-up because they receive hurdle faster
100% catch-up is illegal under SEBI AIF Regulations
Both have identical LP impact; only GP economics differ
LPs prefer 50% partial catch-up because more of the above-hurdle residual is shared between LP and GP, reducing the GP's share of residual profits

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6: higher catch-up rate = more of residual profits to Manager = HIGHER risk to LPs of receiving a reduced (or zero) share of above-hurdle residual until GP reaches its catch-up target. A 50% partial catch-up LEAVES more for LPs during the catch-up layer, so option D is the LP-preferred outcome and is the keyed correct answer. The Trap: A reverses the preference; B is wrong because catch-up is permitted under SEBI AIF Regulations (the illegality framing does not apply); C is false because LP economics shift materially with the catch-up percentage. Note: Corrected the trap labels so the keyed option D is not mis-described as false. Removed the anchor-LP negotiation pro-tip and the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, since those negotiation tactics go beyond the workbook's catch-up discussion on p.126.
